calls.head: The Stars will send Heiskanen and Harley at Scheifele
calls.body: At home, the Stars keep sending Heiskanen and Harley out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Glen Gulutzan has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Jets’ first line is Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti.

calls.head: Don’t buy Skinner’s slump against the Stars
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Skinner has been shaky against the Stars, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Skinner starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .901 than to his .832 against the Stars.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Robertson reaches 500 points as the Stars beat the Jets
paras: What a finish. Wyatt Johnston opened the scoring for the Stars early in the second, with Jason Robertson picking up his 500th NHL point on the assist. Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor scored less than two minutes apart midway through the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Roope Hintz made it 2-2 for Dallas with two minutes left. Hintz won it with his second goal of the night in overtime.

The Stars carried the play, outshooting the Jets 38-19, but needed overtime to win it. Jake Oettinger made 17 saves for the Stars, and Stuart Skinner stopped 35 of 38. By our Swing measure, Dylan Samberg had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Hintz’s overtime winner in the game.
Neither power play scored: the Stars killed all four Jets power plays, and the Jets killed both of Dallas’. The Stars moved to 6-3-1, and the Jets fell to 4-3-3.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Stars.
The Jets are winless in four (0-2-2).
The Jets’ Mario Ferraro played his 500th NHL game.
The Stars have beaten the Jets five straight times, going back to last season.
